request.prompt:
You are clustering code review findings from the same PR. For each PAIR below, decide whether the two findings describe the SAME underlying issue — same root cause in the same code location. Different wording is fine. A finding about a DIFFERENT defect in the same file or function is NOT the same issue. Severity or aspect differences of the same root cause ARE the same issue.


For THIS scoring pass, duplicate equivalence is stricter than sharing a root cause.
You must compare the COMPLETE MATERIAL CLAIMS, including mechanism, triggering
conditions, execution path, and consequence. The same line or broad concern does
not establish equivalence. A report of wrong-category selection, a case/rename
mismatch, a crash, and a silent fallback are different claims even at one lookup.
An inactive/unbound API concern and an alleged active user-facing failure differ.
A compound report with an additional material claim does NOT equal its subset.
Differences only in wording, severity, or hedging do not create separate claims.
If the claimed mechanisms, triggers or consequences conflict, or one report adds
an unsupported/different material factual claim, return same=false. You are NOT
verifying which claim is true; do not repair or reinterpret either report to make
them match. If unsure whether their full claims are equivalent, return false.

For every numbered pair, extract what A and B actually CLAIM into mechanism,
trigger and consequence. Then list material_differences and give your equivalence
verdict, confidence and reason. same=true requires no material differences.
Return ONLY this JSON object, with EVERY pair index exactly once:
{"pairs":[{"pair":1,"a":{"mechanism":"...","trigger":"...","consequence":"..."},"b":{"mechanism":"...","trigger":"...","consequence":"..."},"material_differences":[],"same":true,"confidence":0.9,"reason":"..."}]}

A: No frontend tests for the new admin embedding UI: the component's save/cancel flows, buffered rollback on cancel, the adapter's hardcoded pathFor, and the ADMIN_MODELS/basePath change routing embeddable-host requests to /admin/ are only verifiable manually
B: Zero frontend tests for the entire new admin embedding UI, including the pathFor override, the ADMIN_MODELS basePath change shared by all admin models, addHost/deleteHost, the buffered save/cancel/delete flows, the post-save client-side category patch, and the store hydration the page depends on (plural *_ids hydration tested only via the single-word 'color' fixture, not the real multi-word 'embeddable_host_ids' consumer)

A: The migration dereferences [0] on a SELECT that returns no rows whenever no site_settings row named 'embed_category' has a value exactly matching a live category name — the case for every fresh install (site_settings is empty while migrations run) and every site that never set embed_category or whose named category was renamed/deleted — so execute(...)[0]['id'] raises and aborts the migration. db:migrate fails mid-upgrade (IndexError/NoMethodError on the empty result), blocking the upgrade entirely; the `if category_id == 0` uncategorized fallback the author wrote is unreachable dead code because [0] raises before it can ever yield 0 — the same file guards its other lookup with cmd_tuples > 0 but leaves this one unguarded.
B: Data migration create_embeddable_hosts (20150818190757) crashes with NoMethodError when the 'embed_category' site setting row doesn't exist — the default state for most installs since Discourse persists only overridden settings — aborting db:migrate on upgrade; it crashes the same way when the stored value doesn't match a category name, and the 'if category_id == 0' fallback to uncategorized_category_id is unreachable dead code
